facts: Displacement is a vector, while the distance between the two positions is its magnitude, a single number.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t_{2})-\underset{\sim}{r}(t_{1})$ subtracts the earlier position from the later one, in that order.
Reversing the order reverses the vector, so the two answers differ only by a minus sign.
For a displacement $a\underset{\sim}{i}+b\underset{\sim}{j}$, the distance between the positions is $\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$.
The displacement is the straight-line change in position, not the distance travelled along a curved path.
A zero displacement means the particle has returned to where it started.
The direction is the angle measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis, found from $\tan\theta=\dfrac{b}{a}$.
steps: Find the position vector at each of the two times.
Subtract the earlier position vector from the later one.
If a distance or a direction is asked for, find the magnitude or the angle of that displacement.

foundation.question_text:

Find its displacement from $t=1$ to $t=4$.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+5t\underset{\sim}{j}$.

How far apart are its positions at $t=0$ and $t=3$?

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(3t-1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(4t+2)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
How far apart are its positions at $t=1$ and $t=3$?

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+3t\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Find the direction of its displacement from $t=1$ to $t=2$, as an angle measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(5-t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Find its displacement from $t=0$ to $t=3$.

Its displacement from $t=1$ to a later time $T$ is $12\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Its displacement from $t=2$ to a later time $T$ is $21\underset{\sim}{i}+18\underset{\sim}{j}$.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t-5)\underset{\sim}{i}+t^{2}\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Find the exact distance between its positions at $t=1$ and $t=3$.

A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(10-t^{2})\underset{\sim}{i}+4t\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Find the direction of its displacement from $t=1$ to $t=3$, as an angle measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{r}(1)=9\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(3)=\underset{\sim}{i}+12\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(3)-\underset{\sim}{r}(1)=-8\underset{\sim}{i}+8\underset{\sim}{j}$
The displacement points left and up, so it lies in the second quadrant.
$\theta=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}$
$=135^{\circ}$
